checklist.title: Verify Computational Complexity Bounds: Does compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff complete within block processing time budget under maximum blob load?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff function implementation (SG-019). 2. Determine the current algorithmic complexity - verify if O(n^2) reference or O(n log n) FK20 is used. 3. Benchmark execution time with MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK blobs submitted in a single block. 4. Measure total computation time against block processing time budget. 5. Submit transactions with maximum allowed blobs per block repeatedly to stress test. 6. Monitor for any processing delays or timeouts under sustained high blob throughput. 7. Verify that validation layers (MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK limit) are enforced before computation begins. 8. Attempt to bypass blob count limits through malformed or edge-case transactions.
checklist.falsification_test: Submit a block containing MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK blobs and measure if compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff exceeds the block processing time budget. If it does, the invariant is violated.
checklist.attack_scenario: An attacker submits transactions containing the maximum allowed number of blobs per block. If the implementation uses O(n^2) complexity instead of O(n log n) FK20, sustained high blob throughput could cause unacceptable delays in block processing, potentially leading to consensus delays or node resource exhaustion.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054, Primary Element: SG-019:compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff, Type: invariant. The property requires timing verification under load. The O(n^2) reference implementation is explicitly noted as potentially vulnerable during high blob throughput.

checklist.title: Verify FK20 Algorithm Implementation: Is O(n log n) complexity algorithm used instead of O(n^2) reference implementation?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Review the source code of compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff (SG-019). 2. Identify the algorithm used - check for FK20 implementation markers. 3. Analyze loop structures and complexity characteristics. 4. Verify that no O(n^2) fallback paths exist in the implementation. 5. Run benchmarks with varying blob counts (1, 2, 4, 8, ... MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK) and plot execution time to verify O(n log n) scaling. 6. Compare benchmark results against theoretical O(n^2) vs O(n log n) curves to confirm algorithm choice.
checklist.falsification_test: Measure execution time for compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff with doubling input sizes. If execution time grows quadratically (4x for 2x input) rather than linearithmically (~2x for 2x input), the implementation uses O(n^2) complexity.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054, Supporting check for algorithm verification. The SHOULD requirement for FK20 algorithm indicates this is a recommended but potentially not mandatory optimization.

checklist.title: Verify MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK Limit Enforcement: Is the blob count limit properly validated before KZG proof computation?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify where MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK validation occurs in the transaction processing pipeline. 2. Verify validation happens BEFORE compute_cells_and_kzg_proofs_polynomialcoeff is invoked. 3. Attempt to submit transactions with blob counts exceeding MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK. 4. Test edge cases: exactly MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK, MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK + 1, integer overflow attempts. 5. Verify that rejected transactions do not trigger partial KZG computation. 6. Check for any code paths that could bypass the blob count validation.
checklist.falsification_test: Attempt to submit a block with more than MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK blobs through various means (direct submission, split transactions, malformed headers). If any submission triggers KZG computation for excess blobs, the validation layer is bypassed.
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054, Validation layer check. The MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK limit is the primary defense against computational DoS attacks targeting KZG proof generation.
